title: The 2014 Algorithm Invoice
subtitle: Southern Trust · Estate Planning · Documentary Boundaries
description: A February 2013 draft, a July 2014 invoice-form document, and a 2026 Senate letter reproducing a same-day 2014 reported wire receipt are compared as distinct records. A matching amount and date do not by themselves prove invoice allocation or algorithm delivery.

sources.title: Southern Trust algorithms invoice document
sources.note: One-page Southern Trust invoice addressed to Leon Black, containing an unfilled bracketed entity placeholder. It describes $20 million in estate-planning-related algorithms. Does not by itself establish settlement, delivery, or actual system operation. Avoid reproducing banking details.

sources.title: Revised draft estate-planning service letter
sources.note: Archive-indexed February 11, 2013; header identifies February 6 revisions to a February 5 lawyer's draft. Draft terms describe a conditional $23.5 million estate-planning fee to Southern Trust. Does not establish execution, payment, algorithm development, or relation to the July 2014 invoice.

sources.title: Senate Finance letter reproducing July 2014 wire receipt email
sources.citation: Senate Finance letter (Mar 20 2026), p. 3; cites EFTA01915809
sources.note: A letter from Senator Ron Wyden includes an embedded image of July 15, 2014 correspondence. In that image Richard Kahn reports a $20 million wire received in Southern Trust Company. The letter points to DOJ EFTA01915809. The DOJ original was not independently retrieved here. The email does not identify the July 2014 algorithm invoice, show bank settlement documents, or establish algorithm delivery.

sources.title: DOJ original PDF locator for July 2014 reported receipt email
sources.note: The Senate Finance letter cites this DOJ DataSet 10 PDF as the underlying document for a July 15, 2014 email reporting $20 million received by Southern Trust. The original PDF was not independently downloaded during this research; this registry item records the citation URL, not independent authentication.

edges.label: named invoice addressee
edges.summary: The Southern Trust invoice document names Leon Black as the addressee and contains a placeholder for which Black entity would be invoiced. This is not a verified completed payment.

edges.summary: The document describes a $20 million fee for algorithms for estate planning and related purposes. This is a description of a claimed service, not evidence of software delivery.

events.title: Revised estate-planning service letter appears in released records
events.description: Draft dated February 2013 describes conditional $23.5 million fee terms. Archive index date is not proof of signing; the draft is not itself a payment record.

events.title: Southern Trust invoice document references algorithms
events.description: A one-page record describes $20 million in algorithms for estate planning. An unfilled placeholder appears in the recipient field; settlement and delivery are unverified.

events.title: 2014 wire-receipt email reproduced in a 2026 Senate letter
events.description: The 2026 Senate Finance letter reproduces an image of a July 15, 2014 Kahn email saying a $20 million wire was received in STC. This is documentary correspondence reporting a receipt, not independently obtained bank settlement or proof the specific invoice was paid.

hypotheses.question: Was the stated algorithm service actually delivered or paid for?
hypotheses.context: The document identifies an amount and a broad service description but does not show implementation or payment.
hypotheses.forEvidence: An invoice document exists identifying parties and a service category.
hypotheses.againstEvidence: A bracketed placeholder and lack of payment confirmation, agreement scope, code records, or delivery acceptance prevent a definitive operational conclusion.
hypotheses.nextCheck: Locate the signed agreement, final recipient entity, invoice settlement record, work product, and independent service delivery evidence.

hypotheses.question: Did the 2013 draft and 2014 algorithm invoice refer to the same engagement?
hypotheses.context: Both name Southern Trust and Leon Black in an estate-planning context, but their amounts, dates and documentary forms differ.
hypotheses.forEvidence: The same broad counterparties and estate-planning subject occur in a 2013 draft and a 2014 invoice document.
hypotheses.againstEvidence: A revised unsigned draft cannot establish a finalized 2013 contract, and the 2014 invoice retains an unfinished entity placeholder. No explicit amendment or cross-reference has been identified.
hypotheses.nextCheck: Find a fully executed agreement, amendment, final invoice and payment records explicitly linking the terms. Do not add their dollar amounts together.

hypotheses.question: Was the July 15, 2014 reported $20 million wire allocated to the same-day estate-planning algorithm invoice?
hypotheses.context: The July 15 invoice and a same-day Kahn email reproduced by the U.S. Senate Finance Committee describe $20 million and Southern Trust, but no invoice number links the documents.
hypotheses.forEvidence: Matching date, amount and receiving institution are reported in different types of records.
hypotheses.againstEvidence: The invoice's billed-entity placeholder is unfilled, and the email excerpt lacks the invoice number, signed engagement scope, and bank settlement reference.
hypotheses.nextCheck: Retrieve DOJ EFTA01915809 and the underlying bank debit/credit records. Confirm invoice allocation through an explicit remittance reference or receiving-party bookkeeping and seek independent service-delivery proof.

traceSteps.title: A revised estate-planning draft proposed conditional fees
traceSteps.established: A draft service letter identifies Southern Trust and Leon Black, with conditional estate-planning fees totaling $23.5 million. The archive indexes it February 11, 2013, while the header identifies February 6 revisions.
traceSteps.notEstablished: Whether the draft was executed, any money was settled, software was produced, or it constituted the same agreement as the July 2014 algorithms invoice.

traceSteps.title: A $20 million invoice document is dated July 15, 2014
traceSteps.established: Southern Trust produced a document addressed to Leon Black describing algorithms for estate planning and related purposes.
traceSteps.notEstablished: Whether the document was final, paid, or linked to delivered algorithmic services.

traceSteps.title: A July 2014 email reportedly confirms a $20 million wire received by Southern Trust
traceSteps.established: A March 2026 Senate Finance letter reproduces a July 15, 2014 email image in which Richard Kahn says a $20 million wire was received in Southern Trust Company.
traceSteps.notEstablished: That the reported receipt settled the specific July 15 algorithm invoice, who remitted the wire as shown on bank records, or that algorithmic services were delivered.
